desc: Ideation: closure/fixed-point structure, D/E transform, doubling bound, DSU merge-tree approach identified as intended solution.
Formally define reqL/reqR and merge formulas (sum' = sumC+sumD; reqL' = max(reqL_C, reqL_D - sumC); reqR' = max(reqR_D, reqR_C - sumD)); absorbable iff S > req.

Prove key lemma: at merge time the absorbing side's sum exceeds the absorbed side's req (edges processed in increasing absorbed-value order; equal values never merge — matches strict inequality); merge tree well-defined.
Validate algorithm by hand on Sample 1 (→ 4 30 2 13 2 13) and Sample 2 spot checks (K=3→235, K=1→22, K=2→47, K=5→31, K=12→235).
Implement merge-tree construction: directed edges, sort by absorbed value, DSU components storing sum/reqL/reqR/leaf bounds, internal nodes with children + absorbing side.
Complexity audit of Step 3: per-leaf climbing is Θ(N²) worst case (decreasing array builds chain; leaf k climbs N-1-k nodes) — must replace with downward propagation.
Edge-case verification: found DSU path compression corrupts tree parent pointers (wrong answers, e.g. leaf 1 in [3,2,1] would give 2 instead of 3) — must separate dsu[] from tparent[].
Rewrite code: separate dsu[] (compression) from tparent[] (tree links); implement O(N) bottom-up reach[] + top-down final[] propagation; handle forest roots.
Verify rewritten code: mentally run Sample 1, Sample 2, decreasing array [3,2,1] (expect 6 3 1), all-equal array, N=2 cases.
Final code pass: fast I/O, output format, confirm no recursion depth issues.
